title: Xanthomonas citri pv. citri findings in imported citrus fruit consignments in the Netherlands
extra_json: {"keyword":"","organism_label":"","organism_name":"","organism_strain":"","project_acc":"PRJEB65884","project_data_type":"Genome sequencing and assembly","project_description":"Citrus bacterial canker (CBC), caused by Xanthomonas citri pv. citri and pv. aurantifolii, presents a major risk to the Mediterranean citrus producing areas of the European Union (EU). title: Xanthomonas campestris pv. musacearum NCPPB2251 Genome Sequencing
extra_json: {"keyword":"","organism_label":"","organism_name":"Xanthomonas vasicola pv. musacearum NCPPB 2251","organism_strain":"NCPPB 2251","project_acc":"PRJNA163287","project_data_type":"Genome sequencing and assembly","project_description":"The bacterium Xanthomonas campestris pathovar musacearum (Xcm) is the causal agent of banana Xanthomonas wilt (BXW). This disease has devastated economies based on banana and plantain crops (Musa species) in East Africa. Xcm was first described as a wilt-causing pathogen on enset (Ensente ventricosum), a plant closely related to banana that is a staple crop in the highlands of Ethiopia. In 1974 the Yirgou and Bradbury wrote that “Great care should be taken to see that enset wilt does not escape and establish itself on banana in other parts of the world where it could pose a serious problem on this crop”. Ominously, one and a half decades later, a major epidemic of this disease was reported in Uganda .  Subsequently it has spread into many banana-growing regions around the Great Lakes in Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Democratic Republic of Congo, Rwanda and Burundi . Efforts are underway to tackle this pathogen by a number of different measures including cultural practices and genetic modification of the crop. Although classified as a member of the species Xanthomonas campestris, we recently showed that Xcm is more properly considered to be derived from the species Xanthomonas vasicola. We previously generated complete genome sequences for a single isolate of Xcm from banana in Uganda and for a single isolate of X. vasicola pathovar vasculorum (Xvv) that is non-pathogenic on banana and was isolated from sugarcane in South Africa. These two isolates share identical gyrase B DNA sequences. Differences between these two genome sequences revealed several candidate genes that might play a role in adaptation to the banana host. These may also be useful tools in identifying genes for deployment of disease resistance. Specifically, these included homologues of effectors secreted and translocated by the type III secretion system (T3SS). T3SS effectors have previously been shown to contribute to host-specificity acting as virulence and/or avirulence factors [refs]. Previous work showed that Xcm is a highly monomorphic pathogen and no specific genetic differences have yet been detected among different isolates using traditional typing and diagnostic methods . Affordable complete genome sequencing now makes it feasible to discover previously hidden genetic diversity among isolates of a monomorphic pathogen, though this approach has rarely been applied to phytopathogens as yet. Here we use genome-wide sequence data to discover a set of single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) among East African isolates of Xcm. These SNPs have potential as molecular markers for phylogeographic studies of the epidemiology and spread of the pathogen. Our analysis suggests the presence of at least two major sub-lineages of the pathogen; Xcm isolates from Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania and Burundi are genetically distinct from isolates collected in Ethiopia, DR Congo and Rwanda, suggesting that the current outbreaks of BXW on Musa species in the region have more than one origin.","project_id":163287,"project_method":"","project_methodtype":"Sequencing","project_name":"Xanthomonas vasicola pv. musacearum NCPPB 2251","project_objectives_list":[{"project_objectives":"","project_objectivestype":"Assembly"},{"project_objectives":"","project_objectivestype":"Variation"}],"project_subtype":"","project_target_capture":"Whole","project_target_material":"Genome","project_target_scope":"Monoisolate","project_title":"Xanthomonas campestris pv. musacearum NCPPB2251 Genome Sequencing","project_type":"Primary submission","registration_date":"2015/07/31 00:00","relevance_agricultural":"yes","relevance_environmental":"","relevance_evolution":"","relevance_industrial":"","relevance_medical":"","relevance_model":"","relevance_other":"","sequencing_status":"Contigs","sort_by_datatype":1007630,"sort_by_organism":743063,"sort_by_projecttype":1010170,"submitter_organization":"University of Exeter","submitter_organization_list":["University of Exeter"],"supergroup":"Bacteria","taxid":1184256,"uid":"163287"}

title: Diagnostic and epidemiological tools for the Xanthomonas hortorum species-level clade based on OMICs technologies
extra_json: {"keyword":"","organism_label":"","organism_name":"","organism_strain":"","project_acc":"PRJEB38824","project_data_type":"","project_description":"Despite its recent re-emergence and increased prevalence in many countries, the research on Xanthomonas hortorum species-level clade members has been very limited until now. It is thus important to have an increased knowledge thereof to be able to react to its increasing occurrence. Therefore, the overall aim of the present project is to study the genomic diversity of the different pathovars within the X. hortorum species-level clade in order to design novel diagnostic methods and to study the molecular base of host-specificity of the individual pathovars. Genomic data of X. hortorum species-level clade members are largely unavailable, and this project aims at filling that substantial gap. By establishing the genome sequences of representative isolates from this clade, this project will also fill in an important information gap with insights on population ecology, virulence, genetics and evolution. This will also allow designing genomics informed assays for rapid, easy and in-field diagnostics in order to contribute to a prevention of further spreading/introduction of these pathogens. title: Xanthomonas campestris pv. musacearum NCPPB4434 Genome Sequencing
extra_json: {"keyword":"","organism_label":"NCPPB4434","organism_name":"Xanthomonas vasicola pv. musacearum NCPPB 4434","organism_strain":"NCPPB4434","project_acc":"PRJNA163299","project_data_type":"Genome sequencing","project_description":"Although classified as a member of the species Xanthomonas campestris, we recently showed that Xcm is more properly considered to be derived from the species Xanthomonas vasicola. We previously generated complete genome sequences for a single isolate of Xcm from banana in Uganda and for a single isolate of X. vasicola pathovar vasculorum (Xvv) that is non-pathogenic on banana and was isolated from sugarcane in South Africa. These two isolates share identical gyrase B DNA sequences. Differences between these two genome sequences revealed several candidate genes that might play a role in adaptation to the banana host. These may also be useful tools in identifying genes for deployment of disease resistance. Specifically, these included homologues of effectors secreted and translocated by the type III secretion system (T3SS). T3SS effectors have previously been shown to contribute to host-specificity acting as virulence and/or avirulence factors . Previous work showed that Xcm is a highly monomorphic pathogen and no specific genetic differences have yet been detected among different isolates using traditional typing and diagnostic methods . Affordable complete genome sequencing now makes it feasible to discover previously hidden genetic diversity among isolates of a monomorphic pathogen, though this approach has rarely been applied to phytopathogens as yet. Here we use genome-wide sequence data to discover a set of single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) among East African isolates of Xcm. These SNPs have potential as molecular markers for phylogeographic studies of the epidemiology and spread of the pathogen. Our analysis suggests the presence of at least two major sub-lineages of the pathogen; Xcm isolates from Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania and Burundi are genetically distinct from isolates collected in Ethiopia, DR Congo and Rwanda, suggesting that the current outbreaks of BXW on Musa species in the region have more than one origin.","project_id":163299,"project_method":"","project_methodtype":"Sequencing","project_name":"Xanthomonas vasicola pv. musacearum NCPPB 4434","project_objectives_list":[{"project_objectives":"","project_objectivestype":"Assembly"},{"project_objectives":"","project_objectivestype":"Variation"}],"project_subtype":"","project_target_capture":"Whole","project_target_material":"Genome","project_target_scope":"Monoisolate","project_title":"Xanthomonas campestris pv. musacearum NCPPB4434 Genome Sequencing","project_type":"Primary submission","registration_date":"2012/05/05 00:00","relevance_agricultural":"yes","relevance_environmental":"","relevance_evolution":"","relevance_industrial":"","relevance_medical":"","relevance_model":"","relevance_other":"","sequencing_status":"SRA/Trace","sort_by_datatype":1007624,"sort_by_organism":743075,"sort_by_projecttype":1010164,"submitter_organization":"University of Exeter","submitter_organization_list":["University of Exeter"],"supergroup":"Bacteria","taxid":1184262,"uid":"163299"}

title: A new multi-level genome typing scheme for X.citri
extra_json: {"keyword":"","organism_label":"","organism_name":"","organism_strain":"","project_acc":"PRJNA1232944","project_data_type":"Raw sequence reads","project_description":"Xanthomonas citri is a phytopathogenic bacterium associated with diverse plant hosts and causes a wide range of economically significant plant diseases. Historically, its identification was based upon host plant association and disease symptoms. Additionally, numerous typing and classification systems such as pathovar, phylogroup, pathotype and race have been used to classify X. citri subgroups. DNA-based methods, such as genomics, can not only identify X. citri subgroups but also provide highly discriminative typing useful for epidemiology and disease control. Here, we developed a unified Multilevel Genome Typing (MGT) scheme for classifying X. citri at population and outbreak levels with a focus on pv. malvacearum. MGT builds upon classical multilocus sequence typing (MLST) and incorporates multiple levels with increasing numbers of loci for improved identification and monitoring of pathogens at different levels. Our X. citri MGT consists of eight levels, from the lowest level (MGT1) that builds on 7 loci equivalent to classical MLST to MGT7 consisting of 2,027 loci representing X. citri core genes, and the highest level, MGT8 consisting of all genes and intergenic regions of the pv. malvacearum core genome (3,977 loci). We constructed the X. citri MGT scheme using 415 genomes, with lower levels, MGT2 and MGT3, associated with genetic lineages, pathotypes and races of pvs fuscans, citri and malvacearum that were isolated from different regions. Higher levels (MGT4-8) require increasing numbers of loci and discrimination of related X. citri clusters as scheme level increases, with the highest level, MGT8, allowing for tracing of highly similar isolates consistent with an outbreak cluster. title: Comparison of genomic sequences and virulence functions of two Xanthomonas strains
extra_json: {"keyword":"","organism_label":"","organism_name":"Xanthomonas campestris","organism_strain":"","project_acc":"PRJNA13900","project_data_type":"","project_description":"  Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris. This organism is the causative agent of crucifer black rot disease, which has an enormous impact on worldwide agriculture. Comparison of these two strains reveals different pathogenic properties on host plants, with ATCC 33913 showing wak virulence on cabbage and radish plants.    Comparison of the two genomes expected to show differences in their content. A surprising finding was a massive chromosomal inversion between the two strains that appears to have occurred due to recombination between two insertion sequences (IS1478). Other strain-specific differences included single-nucleotide polymorphisms (3548) in 498 genes, insertions and deletions, and strain-specific chromosomal islands which appear to have been acquired by horizontal gene transfer as inferred by the presence of phage-specific proteins and a difference in GC-content and codon usage. Strain 8004 has two type IV secretion proteins, XC2031 and XC2040, and some transport proteins, XC2405, XC2294, and SC2295 that are specific for that strain.    A number of transposition mutants were used to identify virulence functions. A total of 75 nonredundant mutants were obtained, some in what are presumably virulence-related genes (39) and some in intergenic regions that may have affected regulation of downsteam genes (11). title: Transcriptome investigation shed light into the role of volatile organic compounds in the growth inhibition of Xanthomonas species
extra_json: {"keyword":"","organism_label":"","organism_name":"Xanthomonas albilineans","organism_strain":"","project_acc":"PRJNA1032123","project_data_type":"Transcriptome or Gene expression","project_description":"X. albilineans is one of the most important phytobacteria species which affect sugarcane production. Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) produced by microorganisms may have a noteworthy role in the control of plant diseases. extra_json: {"keyword":"","organism_label":"","organism_name":"","organism_strain":"","project_acc":"PRJEB38824","project_data_type":"","project_description":"Despite its recent re-emergence and increased prevalence in many countries, the research on Xanthomonas hortorum species-level clade members has been very limited until now. It is thus important to have an increased knowledge thereof to be able to react to its increasing occurrence. Therefore, the overall aim of the present project is to study the genomic diversity of the different pathovars within the X. hortorum species-level clade in order to design novel diagnostic methods and to study the molecular base of host-specificity of the individual pathovars. Genomic data of X. hortorum species-level clade members are largely unavailable, and this project aims at filling that substantial gap. By establishing the genome sequences of representative isolates from this clade, this project will also fill in an important information gap with insights on population ecology, virulence, genetics and evolution. This will also allow designing genomics informed assays for rapid, easy and in-field diagnostics in order to contribute to a prevention of further spreading/introduction of these pathogens. title: Xanthomonas citri pv. citri findings in imported citrus fruit consignments in the Netherlands
extra_json: {"keyword":"","organism_label":"","organism_name":"","organism_strain":"","project_acc":"PRJEB65884","project_data_type":"Genome sequencing and assembly","project_description":"Citrus bacterial canker (CBC), caused by Xanthomonas citri pv. citri and pv. aurantifolii, presents a major risk to the Mediterranean citrus producing areas of the European Union (EU). The commercial trade of citrus fruit is recognized as one of the seven significant X. citri pv. citri introduction pathways, however, under the current EU phytosanitary measures the likelihood of introduction of X. citri pv. citri and X. citri pv. aurantifolii in the Mediterranean region with infected fruit is rated unlikely. In order to closely monitor the commercial trade flow of citrus fruit, all imported consignments from outside the EU from 2013-2022 have undergone visual inspection for the presence of CBC symptoms upon entering the Netherlands. Consignments that contained citrus fruits with symptoms that could indicate a X. citri pv citri or X. citri pv. aurantifolii infection were quarantined and a sample of symptomatic fruits per consignment was sent to the laboratory for official analysis. The number of consignments containing such symptomatic citrus fruits increased from only 8 in 2013 to 136 in 2022. Survey results revealed the presence of only X. citri pv. citri in 97 infected consignments in the period 2013-2022. Remarkably, 48 consignments were infected with X. citri pv. citri in 2022 alone, representing a 35.3% of the consignments containing symptomatic citrus fruit, matching the expected CBC symptoms. These X. citri pv. citri infected consignments in the period 2013-2022 primarily referred to fruits of C. latifolia (64), C. hystrix (17) and C. grandis (11) and from several countries in South and Southeast Asia as well as in South America. The increasing number of intercepted consignments containing symptomatic citrus fruits due to the presence of viable and highly pathogenic X citri pv citri strains entering the Netherlands raises concerns about the effectiveness of the post-harvest chemical disinfection treatment implemented in the citrus fruit exporting countries. It additionally puts the role of citrus fruit in the long distance dispersal of X. citri pv. citri under debate. title: Xanthomonas citri pv. citri findings in imported citrus fruit consignments in the Netherlands
extra_json: {"keyword":"","organism_label":"","organism_name":"","organism_strain":"","project_acc":"PRJEB65884","project_data_type":"Genome sequencing and assembly","project_description":"Citrus bacterial canker (CBC), caused by Xanthomonas citri pv. citri and pv. aurantifolii, presents a major risk to the Mediterranean citrus producing areas of the European Union (EU). The commercial trade of citrus fruit is recognized as one of the seven significant X. citri pv. citri introduction pathways, however, under the current EU phytosanitary measures the likelihood of introduction of X. citri pv. citri and X. citri pv. aurantifolii in the Mediterranean region with infected fruit is rated unlikely. In order to closely monitor the commercial trade flow of citrus fruit, all imported consignments from outside the EU from 2013-2022 have undergone visual inspection for the presence of CBC symptoms upon entering the Netherlands. Consignments that contained citrus fruits with symptoms that could indicate a X. citri pv citri or X. citri pv. aurantifolii infection were quarantined and a sample of symptomatic fruits per consignment was sent to the laboratory for official analysis. The number of consignments containing such symptomatic citrus fruits increased from only 8 in 2013 to 136 in 2022. Survey results revealed the presence of only X. citri pv. citri in 97 infected consignments in the period 2013-2022. Remarkably, 48 consignments were infected with X. citri pv. citri in 2022 alone, representing a 35.3% of the consignments containing symptomatic citrus fruit, matching the expected CBC symptoms. extra_json: {"keyword":"","organism_label":"","organism_name":"","organism_strain":"","project_acc":"PRJEB65884","project_data_type":"Genome sequencing and assembly","project_description":"Citrus bacterial canker (CBC), caused by Xanthomonas citri pv. citri and pv. aurantifolii, presents a major risk to the Mediterranean citrus producing areas of the European Union (EU). The commercial trade of citrus fruit is recognized as one of the seven significant X. citri pv. citri introduction pathways, however, under the current EU phytosanitary measures the likelihood of introduction of X. citri pv. citri and X. citri pv. aurantifolii in the Mediterranean region with infected fruit is rated unlikely. In order to closely monitor the commercial trade flow of citrus fruit, all imported consignments from outside the EU from 2013-2022 have undergone visual inspection for the presence of CBC symptoms upon entering the Netherlands. Consignments that contained citrus fruits with symptoms that could indicate a X. citri pv citri or X. citri pv. aurantifolii infection were quarantined and a sample of symptomatic fruits per consignment was sent to the laboratory for official analysis. The number of consignments containing such symptomatic citrus fruits increased from only 8 in 2013 to 136 in 2022. Survey results revealed the presence of only X. citri pv. citri in 97 infected consignments in the period 2013-2022. Remarkably, 48 consignments were infected with X. citri pv. citri in 2022 alone, representing a 35.3% of the consignments containing symptomatic citrus fruit, matching the expected CBC symptoms. These X. citri pv. citri infected consignments in the period 2013-2022 primarily referred to fruits of C. latifolia (64), C. hystrix (17) and C. grandis (11) and from several countries in South and Southeast Asia as well as in South America. The increasing number of intercepted consignments containing symptomatic citrus fruits due to the presence of viable and highly pathogenic X citri pv citri strains entering the Netherlands raises concerns about the effectiveness of the post-harvest chemical disinfection treatment implemented in the citrus fruit exporting countries. It additionally puts the role of citrus fruit in the long distance dispersal of X. citri pv. citri under debate. Appropriate monitoring of the citrus fruit trade flow by visual inspections for the presence of CBC symptoms and subsequent laboratory testing remains a significant tool in reducing the potential risk of the long distance dispersal of X. citri pv. citri.","project_id":1027225,"project_method":"","project_methodtype":"Sequencing","project_name":"Xanthomonas citri pv. citri findings in imported citrus fruit consignments in the Netherlands","project_objectives_list":[{"project_objectives":"Unspecified Objective","project_objectivestype":"Other"}],"project_subtype":"","project_target_capture":"Whole","project_target_material":"Genome","project_target_scope":"Monoisolate","project_title":"Xanthomonas citri pv. citri findings in imported citrus fruit consignments in the Netherlands","project_type":"Primary submission","registration_date":"2023/10/12 00:00","relevance_agricultural":"","relevance_environmental":"","relevance_evolution":"","relevance_industrial":"","relevance_medical":"","relevance_model":"","relevance_other":"","sequencing_status":"Contigs","sort_by_datatype":289483,"sort_by_organism":867757,"sort_by_projecttype":314563,"submitter_organization":"nivip","submitter_organization_list":["nivip"],"supergroup":"","taxid":"","uid":"1027225"}

title: Xanthomonas citri pv. citri findings in imported citrus fruit consignments in the Netherlands
extra_json: {"keyword":"","organism_label":"","organism_name":"","organism_strain":"","project_acc":"PRJEB65884","project_data_type":"Genome sequencing and assembly","project_description":"Citrus bacterial canker (CBC), caused by Xanthomonas citri pv. citri and pv. aurantifolii, presents a major risk to the Mediterranean citrus producing areas of the European Union (EU). The commercial trade of citrus fruit is recognized as one of the seven significant X. citri pv. citri introduction pathways, however, under the current EU phytosanitary measures the likelihood of introduction of X. citri pv. citri and X. citri pv. aurantifolii in the Mediterranean region with infected fruit is rated unlikely. In order to closely monitor the commercial trade flow of citrus fruit, all imported consignments from outside the EU from 2013-2022 have undergone visual inspection for the presence of CBC symptoms upon entering the Netherlands. Consignments that contained citrus fruits with symptoms that could indicate a X. citri pv citri or X. citri pv. aurantifolii infection were quarantined and a sample of symptomatic fruits per consignment was sent to the laboratory for official analysis. The number of consignments containing such symptomatic citrus fruits increased from only 8 in 2013 to 136 in 2022. Survey results revealed the presence of only X. citri pv. citri in 97 infected consignments in the period 2013-2022. Remarkably, 48 consignments were infected with X. citri pv. citri in 2022 alone, representing a 35.3% of the consignments containing symptomatic citrus fruit, matching the expected CBC symptoms. These X. citri pv. citri infected consignments in the period 2013-2022 primarily referred to fruits of C. latifolia (64), C. hystrix (17) and C. grandis (11) and from several countries in South and Southeast Asia as well as in South America. The increasing number of intercepted consignments containing symptomatic citrus fruits due to the presence of viable and highly pathogenic X citri pv citri strains entering the Netherlands raises concerns about the effectiveness of the post-harvest chemical disinfection treatment implemented in the citrus fruit exporting countries. It additionally puts the role of citrus fruit in the long distance dispersal of X. citri pv. citri under debate. Appropriate monitoring of the citrus fruit trade flow by visual inspections for the presence of CBC symptoms and subsequent laboratory testing remains a significant tool in reducing the potential risk of the long distance dispersal of X. citri pv. citri.","project_id":1027225,"project_method":"","project_methodtype":"Sequencing","project_name":"Xanthomonas citri pv. citri findings in imported citrus fruit consignments in the Netherlands","project_objectives_list":[{"project_objectives":"Unspecified Objective","project_objectivestype":"Other"}],"project_subtype":"","project_target_capture":"Whole","project_target_material":"Genome","project_target_scope":"Monoisolate","project_title":"Xanthomonas citri pv. citri findings in imported citrus fruit consignments in the Netherlands","project_type":"Primary submission","registration_date":"2023/10/12 00:00","relevance_agricultural":"","relevance_environmental":"","relevance_evolution":"","relevance_industrial":"","relevance_medical":"","relevance_model":"","relevance_other":"","sequencing_status":"Contigs","sort_by_datatype":289483,"sort_by_organism":867757,"sort_by_projecttype":314563,"submitter_organization":"nivip","submitter_organization_list":["nivip"],"supergroup":"","taxid":"","uid":"1027225"}

title: Xanthomonas citri pv. citri findings in imported citrus fruit consignments in the Netherlands
extra_json: {"keyword":"","organism_label":"","organism_name":"","organism_strain":"","project_acc":"PRJEB65884","project_data_type":"Genome sequencing and assembly","project_description":"Citrus bacterial canker (CBC), caused by Xanthomonas citri pv. citri and pv. aurantifolii, presents a major risk to the Mediterranean citrus producing areas of the European Union (EU). The commercial trade of citrus fruit is recognized as one of the seven significant X. citri pv. citri introduction pathways, however, under the current EU phytosanitary measures the likelihood of introduction of X. citri pv. citri and X. citri pv. aurantifolii in the Mediterranean region with infected fruit is rated unlikely. In order to closely monitor the commercial trade flow of citrus fruit, all imported consignments from outside the EU from 2013-2022 have undergone visual inspection for the presence of CBC symptoms upon entering the Netherlands. Consignments that contained citrus fruits with symptoms that could indicate a X. citri pv citri or X. citri pv. aurantifolii infection were quarantined and a sample of symptomatic fruits per consignment was sent to the laboratory for official analysis. The number of consignments containing such symptomatic citrus fruits increased from only 8 in 2013 to 136 in 2022. Survey results revealed the presence of only X. citri pv. citri in 97 infected consignments in the period 2013-2022. Remarkably, 48 consignments were infected with X. citri pv. citri in 2022 alone, representing a 35.3% of the consignments containing symptomatic citrus fruit, matching the expected CBC symptoms. These X. citri pv. citri infected consignments in the period 2013-2022 primarily referred to fruits of C. latifolia (64), C. hystrix (17) and C. grandis (11) and from several countries in South and Southeast Asia as well as in South America. The increasing number of intercepted consignments containing symptomatic citrus fruits due to the presence of viable and highly pathogenic X citri pv citri strains entering the Netherlands raises concerns about the effectiveness of the post-harvest chemical disinfection treatment implemented in the citrus fruit exporting countries. It additionally puts the role of citrus fruit in the long distance dispersal of X. citri pv. citri under debate. extra_json: {"keyword":"","organism_label":"","organism_name":"","organism_strain":"","project_acc":"PRJNA865108","project_data_type":"Genome sequencing and assembly","project_description":"Bacterial blight caused by Xanthomonas citri pv. punicae (Xcp) severely hit the pomegranate production. Producing complete, circular genomes is important to understand how this bacterium functions. Our study aimed to investigate the Xcp by performing whole genome sequencing of nine isolates in the Illumina platform and hybrid assemblies of Xcp1 isolate using a combination of Illumina and Oxford Nanopore reads to produce closed genome sequences. Like other xanthomonads, Xcp uses type 3 secretion systems (T3SS) to deliver key pathogenicity effectors to host cells. Other accessory genes are often present in mobile genetic elements viz., transposons and plasmids which are important drivers for the survival and pathogenesis of Xcp.
